Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: There is no explicit marker for the absolutive case.
curated_comment: Nêlêmwa (bala1316, ISO nee, Austronesian, New Caledonia) shows ergative alignment documented in Bril (2002) [source cited as Ozanne-Rivierre 1998 in original xlsx, but the PDF is Bril 2002 — same author's full grammar]. Agent markers are 'an' (common NPs in VSO) and 'ru' (focused/oblique NPs). Key correction from original annotation: GB409_16 changed 1→0. Bril (2002: §3.7.1, p.57) states explicitly that thematized transitive subjects appear without agent markers ('Le sujet thématisé du verbe transitif apparaît sans les marques d'agent an ou ru'). GB409_2,3=0 confirmed: 1st/2nd person pronouns lack distinct ergative forms. GB409_22=1 confirmed: thematization conditioning is the additional factor. GB409_23=1 confirmed: 'an' derived from possessive/genitive. GB409_24=1 confirmed: 'ru' = ERG = INST (p.153). Glottocode bala1316 is correct; the previously proposed nele1239 does not exist in Glottolog.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: First-person pronouns do not show a distinct ergative form; the same pronoun form is used for transitive A and intransitive S.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: Second-person pronouns do not show a distinct ergative form; the same pronoun form is used for transitive A and intransitive S.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: Third-person pronouns show ergative alignment; distinct agent forms exist.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs exhibit ergative alignment with agent markers 'an' (common NPs) and 'ru' (oblique/focused NPs).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in the imperfective aspect.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in the perfective aspect.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in past tense clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: Ergative alignment is applied in non-past tenses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in sentences in the indicative mood.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in non-indicative moods.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with realis status.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with irrealis status.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Ergative alignment exists in the context of an agentive A argument.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Ergative alignment exists in the context of a non-agentive A argument.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: When A is thematized (fronted to pre-verbal position), the ergative marker is OBLIGATORILY removed (Bril 2002: §3.7.1, p.57: 'Le sujet thématisé du verbe transitif apparaît sans les marques d'agent an ou ru'). Corrected from original annotation 1→0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: When A is not thematized (basic VSO order), the ergative marker is present.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with an animate A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with an inanimate A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in main clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Non-main clauses exhibit ergative alignment.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Ergative alignment is conditioned by thematization: when A is fronted to initial position (SVO structure), the ergative marker is obligatorily removed. This is the additional conditioning factor.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The agent marker 'an' is historically derived from the possessive/genitive marker; emphatic agent constructions productively combine the agent base with genitive suffixes (Bril 2002: 52). ERG=GEN confirmed.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The agent marker 'ru' (used for focused/oblique agent NPs) also functions as the instrumental marker (Bril 2002: 153). Comitative uses different markers (bole-/ma). ERG=INST confirmed.
